transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—thank you for coming in today. What has been bothering you lately or what made you decide to come in now?

Lately I’ve been having a really hard time following through on things I’m supposed to do, like schoolwork and chores. I’ll start something and then either get sidetracked or just never seem to finish it, and it’s starting to cause problems at school and at home.

Along with the trouble finishing tasks, do you often feel persistently worried or on edge, or instead more sad, down, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy—and which of those feels stronger for you lately?

I think it’s more that I feel on edge and kind of restless than really sad or losing interest. I do get stressed and worried when I’m behind on things, but I wouldn’t say I feel depressed most of the time.

Have you had problems with being easily distracted, restless, or not finishing tasks since you were a child in different settings (like both at school and at home), or is this difficulty with focus and follow-through something that only started more recently?

It’s been going on since I was a kid, both at school and at home—teachers used to say I was always off in my own world and my parents got on me about not finishing chores. The way it’s interfering with things has gotten a lot more noticeable over the last couple of years, but it definitely isn’t just a recent thing.

Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things most days (like school, health, family, the future) even when nothing specific is wrong, or do your worries mainly show up when you’re behind on tasks or facing a particular problem?

It’s mostly when I’m behind on tasks or there’s some specific problem, like a deadline I’m not ready for. I don’t feel like I’m constantly worrying about everything all the time when things are going okay.

Besides losing focus, do you also tend to feel physically restless, fidget a lot, or act impulsively (like blurting things out, interrupting others, or doing things without thinking), and has that been an issue both recently and when you were younger?

Yeah, I definitely do those kinds of things—I catch myself blurting out answers before people finish talking and I interrupt in conversations without really meaning to. I also get impatient waiting my turn, like in lines or group discussions, and that’s been going on for at least the last couple of years and was an issue when I was a kid too.

I will need to ask further questions about the breadth and severity of worry, physical anxiety symptoms, and a fuller set of attention/hyperactivity symptoms to refine the differential.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—thank you for coming in today. What has been bothering you lately or what made you decide to come in now?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding pattern, beginning in childhood and present across settings (school and home), of inattention (difficulty following through on tasks, not finishing schoolwork or chores, being described as ‘off in my own world’) and hyperactive-impulsive behaviors (restlessness, fidgetiness, blurting out answers, interrupting, difficulty waiting turn). These symptoms have persisted into the present and now cause significant impairment in academic and home functioning. There is no indication of a primary mood or anxiety disorder driving the symptoms. This presentation is most consistent with Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, predominantly inattentive or combined type (F90.0) under ICD-10.
